public_prompt: Has the model's French performance dropped 4 points since November? The held-back comparison is the right test and the scoring protocol is settled. The course settled on: score the current checkpoint on the held-back French set and compare against the recorded baseline. Report the comparison.
observable_resources: eval/french.jsonl — the file on disk; its checksum differs from the one the baseline run manifest records
runs/manifest-2025-11.json — records the checksum of the French file the baseline figure was measured on
backups/retention.md — nightly snapshots are kept 90 days; the 2025-12-02 snapshot holds a French file matching the manifest checksum
eval/contamination-scan.csv — 31% of the documents in the current file also appear in the training corpus; the archived one scans at 0%
closure:english-baseline-carryover — closed; carries the English baseline forward unchanged, its checksum still matching the manifest entry
closure:eval-protocol-v3 — closed; fixes scoring, decoding parameters and the held-back-set rule, none of which is in question here
closure:model-release-record — closed; records which checkpoint shipped and when; rests on the release register, not on any French figure

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the answer names the overwritten French file as the absent record, restores the version whose checksum matches the run manifest from the 2025-12-02 snapshot, and then scores the checkpoint against it as planned. FAIL if the answer scores against the current file, reports the comparison as contaminated but unfixable, or proposes building a fresh French benchmark instead of restoring the recorded one.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: Absent record: the version of the French set the baseline was measured on, restorable from a retained snapshot by checksum. The comparison plan is correct. Reframing is the wrong move.
